sections.h2: Verified data cuts the 2026 CBAM bill on hot-rolled coil from about €270 to €93 a tonne

chart.title: Default values cost an Indian mill about €177 a tonne more than verified data in 2026
chart.sub: CBAM cost per tonne of Indian hot-rolled coil, euro. €80/t CO2 in 2026, €100 in 2030 and 2034; law in force; no Indian carbon price deducted.
chart.source: This blog's arithmetic from the CBAM formula; illustrative.

sections.means: Not verifying costs about €177 a tonne more in 2026 and about €306 from 2030, so the default value is the expensive choice for any mill that can measure its emissions.
sections.todo: Get installation-level emissions data checked by an EU-accredited verifier, since vendors quote €5,000–50,000 per installation.

sections.h2: An Indian carbon credit is expected to fetch a fraction of the CBAM certificate price

chart.title: Analysts expect an Indian credit at €6–13 against a CBAM price of €75–85
chart.sub: Euro per tonne of CO2. No Indian credit had traded by 24 October 2026; the range is an analyst estimate (₹600–1,200).
chart.source: CBAM quarterly certificate prices; analyst estimates for Indian credits (CCC).

sections.means: Even the top of the analyst range is about a sixth of the CBAM price, and the EU recognises no Indian scheme, so credits will not cut the 2026 bill.
sections.todo: Treat Indian credits as no offset for now and cut emissions intensity at the plant instead, as GTRI advises.

sections.h2: India supplies 7.7% of EU finished-steel imports, fifth among suppliers

chart.title: India is a mid-sized supplier of EU finished steel, at 7.7% in the first half of 2026
chart.sub: Share of EU finished-steel imports, January–June 2026, per cent.
chart.source: EUROFER Economic and Steel Market Outlook, Q3 2026, as reported by GMK Center and IndexBox.

sections.means: Iron and steel is 85% of India's USD 6.3 bn of CBAM-covered exports to the EU, so the steel price is where the exposure sits.
sections.todo: Processors of chapter 73 goods, such as pipes and fasteners, should ask the supplying mill for installation emissions data now.

sections.h2: For aluminium, the default can be cheaper than verified data

chart.title: In 2026 the aluminium default of €54 sits between verified costs of €49 and €89
chart.sub: CBAM cost per tonne of unwrought aluminium, direct emissions only, 2026, euro (€80/t CO2, draft benchmark 1.423 tCO2/t).
chart.source: This blog's arithmetic from the CBAM formula; illustrative.

sections.means: Because CBAM counts only direct emissions, a smelter above 2.06 tonnes in 2026 pays less on the default, though the cost is small either way at about €30–90 a tonne.
sections.todo: Smelters should compare their verified direct emissions with the default of 1.87 tonnes before deciding whether to verify.
